mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has declined for three consecutive weeks (-16.6 -> -26.4 -> -32.6 -> -36.6), showing strong negative momentum. This autoregressive trend will persist absent an exogenous shock, driving the next-4-week mean below the trailing-4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:four consecutive weeks of declining RETAIL_REC
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's weekly decline reverses and the mean of the next 28 days exceeds the mean of the trailing 28 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained climb in RESIDENTIAL mobility (8.4 -> 19.9 -> 14.3 -> 15.7) signals households spending more time at home, which substitutes directly for retail and recreation trips. Once RESIDENTIAL remains above +15 points for two consecutive weeks, RETAIL_REC should fall further over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above +15 points for 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL at 15.7 in t-0w and 14.3 in t-1w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next 2 weeks despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above +15 for 2+ weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous deep declines in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT (both dropped sharply, WORKPLACES to -50.0 and TRANSIT to -49.3 at t-2w) indicate coordinated suppression of commuting-linked errands. When both series fall together by more than 10 points week-on-week, the combined effect amplifies RETAIL_REC decline beyond either series alone over a 4-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both decline more than 10 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:both series dropped sharply at t-2w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 4-week forward mean is not lower than its trailing mean despite joint WORKPLACES/TRANSIT declines exceeding 10 points, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The partial rebound in WORKPLACES from -50.0 at t-2w to -29.4 at t-0w suggests an early easing of workplace restrictions. If this reopening trend continues for two more consecutive weeks with rises greater than 10 points, retail mobility should recover as commuting-linked shopping resumes.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises for 2 consecutive weeks by more than 10 points
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -50.0 to -29.4 between t-2w and t-0w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES continues rising for 2+ weeks but RETAIL_REC's forward mean remains lower than its trailing mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has declined steadily (-21.7 -> -24.7 -> -27.7 -> -29.7), consistent with a seasonal reduction in outdoor leisure activity. This decline typically co-moves with reduced retail and recreation visits in the immediate following week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined every week over the snapshot
failure_condition: If PARKS stabilizes or rises while RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next week, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM's week-over-week decline has decelerated (from -4.9 to -10.9, then easing to -9.0), suggesting essential-shopping fatigue is stabilizing. If this deceleration persists for two more weeks, it signals broader behavioral normalization that should lift RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM week-over-week change becomes less negative for 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM change eased from -10.9 to -9.0 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM continues to decelerate but RETAIL_REC's forward mean remains lower than its trailing mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous sharp fall in TRANSIT and rise in RESIDENTIAL within the same week indicates active enforcement of stay-at-home policy, which should further compress RETAIL_REC in the immediate next week due to restricted movement.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 15 points week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL rises more than 5 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell to -49.3 and RESIDENTIAL rose to 19.9 at t-2w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises in the week following a joint TRANSIT drop and RESIDENTIAL rise meeting the trigger thresholds, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a sustained lockdown regime, high RESIDENTIAL levels (consistently above +14 for three consecutive weeks) indicate durable behavioral entrenchment that will keep RETAIL_REC suppressed for the next two weeks, unless WORKPLACES simultaneously rebounds signaling a regime change toward reopening.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains above +14 for 3 or more consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL above +14 for the last three weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next 2 weeks despite RESIDENTIAL staying above +14 and WORKPLACES not rebounding, the hypothesis is rejected.
